newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan silent on minister's Bangkok stopover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan silent on minister's Bangkok stopover.

text.p: Taiwan was tight-lipped on Foreign Minister John Chang's unexpected stopover in Bangkok on his way home from Africa, but local media said on Sunday that he discussed economic links with an influential Thai politician.
The mass-circulation United Daily News said the unidentified Thai politican plays a key role in economic and finance matters in Thailand's parliament.
It said the two had a "long discussion" on bilateral economic cooperation.
Chang, originally scheduled to return to Taipei on Friday en route from Bangkok, postponed his return home at the last-minute because of the meeting, the paper said.
The foreign minister also exchanged views with other Thai "friends" about spurring Taiwanese investment in Thailand, the paper said.
Thailand has diplomatic ties with China -- Taiwan's arch-rival -- but maintains business links with Taiwan.
The foreign minister returned to Taipei late on Saturday.

Chang left Taiwan on January 12 for a tour of seven African nations aimed at cementing ties with the region. The visit followed South Africa's announcement in November that it would switch recognition to Beijing from Taipei by the end of 1997.

Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war separated them in 1949. Beijing regards the island as a rebel province ineligible for foreign ties and refuses to have diplomatic ties with countries that recognise Taipei's government.
Taiwan has struggled to break free of the Beijing-engineered diplomatic isolation, often dangling its economic clout as an incentive for countries to set up official or semi-official ties.
